newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada hog inventories rise from year earlier.
newsitem.headline: Canada hog inventories rise from year earlier.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday that hog inventories in Canada were up an estimated 12.1 million head on April 1, a 1.6 percent increase from a year earlier.
Breeding stock numbers rose 1.8 percent, StatsCan said.
Producers in the western provinces reported a record inventory of 5.1 million head, up 2.9 percent from April 1, 1996. In the eastern provinces, inventories increased 0.7 percent, the agency said.
The herd is expanding in Western Canada and accounts for 42.7 percent of the national total, compared with 35.5 percent less than 10 years ago.

The agency said that in Eastern Canada, fewer than one in 10 hogs marketed was exported, compared with one in four in the West. In Canada overall, more than a quarter of the hogs were exported as feeder animals, while the rest were shipped to slaughter houses.
StatsCan said domestic slaughter for the first quarter of 1997 was down 2.1 percent from the same quarter in 1996, and down 5.7 percent from the same quarter in 1995.
The agency said Canadians consumed less pork in 1996 than in the previous year, eating an average of 19.9 kilograms, down from 21.0 kilograms in 1995 and the lowest level since 1990.
